accepted.question_text: For a holomorphic foliation on complex projective space, possibly with singularities, must every leaf accumulate at a singular point of the foliation?

evidence.quote: In the field of holomorphic foliations, even in P2, the following are examples of open basic questions : Do leaves always cluster at singular points ?

accepted.question_text: For generic holomorphic foliations on the complex projective plane P2, what is the topology of a generic leaf?

evidence.quote: In the field of holomorphic foliations, even in P2, the following are examples of open basic questions : Do leaves always cluster at singular points ? What is the topology of generic leaves ? Are leaves dense for generic foliations ?

accepted.question_text: For generic holomorphic foliations on the complex projective plane P2, are generic leaves dense?

evidence.quote: In the field of holomorphic foliations, even in P2, the following are examples of open basic questions : Do leaves always cluster at singular points ? What is the topology of generic leaves ? Are leaves dense for generic foliations ?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold M, let T be an extremal positive ddc-closed current directed by F that gives full mass to the hyperbolic leaves, and for a universal covering map φ_a: D → L of a leaf define the Nevanlinna current τ_r^a. If Theorem 2.1 proves that τ_r^a converges to T for T-almost every a when all singularities of F are linearizable, does the same convergence still hold when the singularities are non-linearizable?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.1 ([10]). In the above situation, assume that all singularities of F are linearizable. Then, for T-almost every a, we have τar → T as r tends to 1, in the sense of currents.
Problem 2.2. (i) Is Theorem 2.1 still true with non-linearizable singularities ? The question here is to estimate the Poincaré metric on leaves near a non-linearizable singularity.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an extremal positive ddc-closed current T directed by a foliation F for which one can estimate the speed at which the Nevanlinna currents τ_r^a converge to T in Theorem 2.1 when tested against smooth observables θ?

evidence.quote: More precisely, for any smooth test form θ of bi-degree (1, 1) on Pk, we have ⟨τar, θ⟩ → ⟨T, θ⟩ as r → 1.
Problem 2.2. (ii) Is there a positive ddc-closed current T, directed by F, extremal, for which one can estimate the speed of the convergence in Theorem 2.1 for smooth observables θ ?

accepted.question_text: Let φ_a: D → L be the universal covering of a leaf, let A(r) = ∫_{D(r)} φ_a^*(ω), and define the associated Ahlfors current by σ_r^a := (1/A(r))(φ_a)_*[D(r)]. Does σ_r^a converge to the extremal positive ddc-closed current T as r tends to 1 for T-almost every base point a?

evidence.quote: Instead of considering the weighted current τar, we can consider an un-weighted current (Ahlfors current) σar := 1/A(r)(φa)∗[D(r)] with A(r) := ∫D(r) φ∗a(ω).
Problem 2.3. Do we have σar → T as r tends to 1 for T-almost every a ?

accepted.question_text: For a leaf parametrized by a universal covering map φ_a: D → L, Theorem 2.1 implies for T-almost every leaf that its Nevanlinna characteristic satisfies T(r) ≥ c log(1/(1-r)) for r close to 1. Does this lower bound hold for every leaf, and in particular does it hold for every leaf when the foliation admits no diffuse ddc-closed current?
accepted.context_brief: uniform lower bound for leaf growth

evidence.quote: A consequence of Theorem 2.1 is that for almost every leaf, with respect to the current T, the Nevanlinna characteristic T(r) for the leaf parametrized by φa, satisfies the inequality T(r) ≥ c log 1/(1 − r) for r close to 1, where c is a positive constant depending on a.
Problem 2.4. Is the above estimate true for every leaf ? In particular, is the above estimate true for every leaf, when there is no diffuse ddc-closed current ?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a foliation of degree d ≥ 2 with non-hyperbolic singularities. Describe the directed positive ddc-closed currents of F, and determine when F can admit diffuse positive closed currents directed by the foliation.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Assume that F is a foliation of degree d ≥ 2 with non-hyperbolic singularities. Describe the ddc-closed positive currents, directed by the foliation. In which case diffuse positive closed currents directed by the foliation do exist ?

accepted.question_text: Let Bd be the parameter space of holomorphic foliations of degree d ≥ 2 and let Bc_d be the subset consisting of foliations that admit directed positive closed currents. Is Bc_d a countable union of proper analytic subsets of Bd?

evidence.quote: Let Bcd denote the set of foliations which admit directed positive closed currents. It is clearly a closed set in Bd.
Problem 3.3. Is the space Bcd a countable union of proper analytic subsets of Bd, when d ≥ 2 ?

accepted.question_text: For a generic foliation in Ad, the space of foliations on an affine chart C2 ⊂ P2 given by polynomial vector fields Z = P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d, or for a generic foliation in Bd, the space of degree-d holomorphic foliations on P2, are generic leaves biholomorphic to the unit disc?

evidence.quote: Let Ad denote the space of foliations given in an affine coordinate chart C2 in P2 by a vector field Z := P(z, w)∂/∂z + Q(z, w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d.
Problem 4.1 (Anosov). For a generic foliation in Ad (resp. Bd), are generic leaves biholomorphic to the unit disc ?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on P2 with finite singular set Sing(F). Is it true that every leaf L of F meets Sing(F)?

evidence.quote: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on P2. Denote by sing(F) the singular set of F which is finite.
Problem 5.1. Is it true that for every leaf L of F, we have L ∩ Sing(F) ̸= ∅ ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Levi-flat hypersurface in P2 that is smooth or real analytic?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2. Does there exist a Levi flat smooth or real analytic hypersurface in P2 ?

accepted.question_text: Assume F is a foliation of geometric degree d ≥ 2 on P2, the line at infinity is invariant, and all singularities are hyperbolic. Do all non-compact leaves of F, meaning all leaves except the compact curves, admit Green functions?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. (i) Assume that F is a foliation of geometric degree d ≥ 2 on P2 with the line at infinity invariant and having only hyperbolic singularities. Do the leaves, except for the compact curves, have Green functions ?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a foliation in Bd with d ≥ 2 that admits a non-zero positive closed current directed by F. What is the resulting function theory of its leaves, especially in terms of the existence and behavior of Green functions?
accepted.context_brief: function theory with directed closed currents

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. (ii) More generally, assume that F is in Bd with d ≥ 2. What is the function theory of leaves (in terms of Green functions), when the foliation admits a non-zero, positive closed current directed by F ?

accepted.question_text: Construct a holomorphic minimal foliation, or a holomorphic minimal lamination, on a compact complex manifold that has uncountably many mutually singular extremal directed currents which are ddc-closed but not closed.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1. Construct holomorphic minimal foliation (resp. lamination) on a compact complex manifold with uncountably many extremal ddc-closed, non-closed, currents directed by the foliation (resp. lamination).

accepted.question_text: Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C2. Can there be one positive-measure set of leaves whose universal covers are C and another positive-measure set of leaves whose universal covers are the unit disc?
accepted.context_brief: mixed parabolic and hyperbolic leaf types

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1. Let Z be a holomorphic vector field in C2. (i) Is it possible to have a set of positive measure of leaves covered by C and another set of positive measure of leaves covered by the unit disc ?

accepted.question_text: Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C2. If a non-pluripolar set of leaves is parabolic, must all leaves be parabolic?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1. Let Z be a holomorphic vector field in C2. (ii) If a non-pluripolar set of leaves are parabolic, are all leaves parabolic ?

accepted.question_text: Find conditions on a holomorphic vector field Z on C2 that guarantee every leaf is covered by the unit disc.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1. Let Z be a holomorphic vector field in C2. (iii) Find conditions which imply that all leaves are covered by the unit disc.

accepted.question_text: Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on Ck that is not the product of a polynomial vector field with a holomorphic function. For a leaf L with uniformization map φ whose source is either C or the unit disc, define the Nevanlinna currents τ_r^φ := (1/T(r))φ_*(log^+(r/|ζ|)). Must every cluster point of τ_r^φ be supported on the hyperplane at infinity, taking r → ∞ in the source-C case and r → 1 in the unit-disc case?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2. Let Z be a holomorphic vector field in Ck which is not the product of a polynomial vector field with a holomorphic function. Let φ be the uniformization of a leaf L. The source could be C or the unit disc. Consider the Nevanlinna currents τφr := 1/T(r) φ∗(log+ r/|ζ|). Are the cluster points of τφr, when r tends to ∞ for the case of C and r tends to 1 for the case of the unit disc, supported necessarily by the hyperplane at infinity ?

accepted.question_text: Let H be the space of entire maps from C to C or to P1 with the compact-open topology, and let U be the subset of maps h such that translates h(z+a_n) can approximate every f in H. What is the minimal possible growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic Th(r) = ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D(t)} h^*(ω) for maps h in U?

evidence.quote: Let H denote the space of entire maps from C to C (resp. to P1), endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Let U be the set of h ∈ H such that for any other function f ∈ H, there is a sequence an ∈ C such that han(z) := h(z + an) converges to f.
Problem 9.1. Find the minimal growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic function Th for h ∈ U , where Th(r) := ∫r0 dt/t ∫D(t) h∗(ω) and ω is the Fubini-Study form on P1.

accepted.question_text: Let H be the space of entire maps as above, and let μ be a non-trivial probability measure on H that is invariant under the translation action h(z) ↦ h(z+a). What can be said about the measure μ(U) of the set U of universal maps with dense translation orbit?

evidence.quote: Recently, Benjamin Weiss has proved the existence of non-trivial probability measures on H which are invariant by the above translation operator, see [30].
Problem 9.2. Given such a measure µ on H as above, what we can say about µ(U ) ?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a complex manifold of dimension n that is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G, let 𝓜 be the space of holomorphic maps from M to Pn with the compact-open topology, and let G act on 𝓜 by precomposition. Under what conditions does this action admit a dense orbit?

evidence.quote: Problem 9.3. Consider a complex manifold M of dimension n which is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G. Let M denote the space of holomorphic maps from M to Pn, endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. The group G acts on this space. (i) Under which conditions this action admits a dense orbit ?

accepted.question_text: In the setting where a Lie group G acts on the space 𝓜 of holomorphic maps from a homogeneous complex manifold M to Pn, extend Benjamin Weiss’s construction of non-trivial invariant probability measures to this broader action.

evidence.quote: Recently, Benjamin Weiss has proved the existence of non-trivial probability measures on H which are invariant by the above translation operator, see [30].

Problem 9.3. Consider a complex manifold M of dimension n which is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G. Let M denote the space of holomorphic maps from M to Pn, endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. The group G acts on this space. (ii) Extend the construction by B. Weiss to this context.

accepted.question_text: Investigate whether the dense-orbit and invariant-measure phenomena discussed above persist for biholomorphisms of Cn and for volume-preserving or symplectic automorphisms of Cn.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.4. Explore the above properties for the following classes of maps in Cn : biholomorphisms of Cn and volume preserving (resp. symplectic) automorphisms of Cn (resp. Cn with n even).

accepted.question_text: For holomorphic foliations on compact Kähler manifolds whose leaves have dimension greater than 1, what is the correct replacement for directed ddc-closed currents of bi-dimension (1,1) used in the one-dimensional case, so that one can develop an ergodic theory for such foliations?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.1. In order to study foliations with leaves of dimension larger than 1, what is the right notion which substitutes directed ddc-closed currents in dimension 1 that should be considered ? Such objects should permit to develop the ergodic theory for these foliations.

accepted.question_text: Construct non-elementary holomorphic foliations F on Pk with leaves of dimension greater than 1 such that no leaf contains a compact curve.

evidence.quote: Problem 10.2. Construct non-elementary foliations F in Pk with leaves of dimension larger than 1 and such that every leaf does not contain a compact curve.

accepted.question_text: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on the unit polydisc Dk ⊂ Ck whose leaves have dimension d > 1 and are tangent to holomorphic (1,0)-forms α1, ..., α_{k-d} that satisfy the Frobenius condition ∂α_j = Σ_{l=1}^{k-d} α_l ∧ β_{j,l}. Can F always be approximated by foliations on Ck or Pk? More precisely, can the forms α_j be approximated uniformly on compact subsets of Dk by entire forms, or by polynomial forms, that still satisfy the same Frobenius condition?

evidence.quote: Let F be a holomorphic foliation in the unit polydisc Dk in Ck. Assume that the leaves of F are of dimension d with d > 1. More precisely, the leaves of F are tangent to a family of k − d holomorphic (1, 0)-forms (αj)1≤j≤k−d on Ck.
These forms αj are linearly independent at a generic point of Dk and satisfy the Frobenius condition ∂αj = Σk−d l=1 αl ∧ βj,l with j = 1, . . . , k − d for some holomorphic (1, 0)-forms βj,l in Dk.

Problem 11.1. Is it always possible to approximate the foliation F by foliations in Ck or Pk ? More precisely, is it always possible to approximate the forms αj, uniformly on compact sets of Dk, by entire forms (resp. polynomial forms) αj,n which still satisfy the above Frobenius condition ?
